headline: Avoiding Common Pitfalls as a First-Time Luxury Home Buyer

publisher.name: Kelby Contreras - Realty ONE Group Evolution

articleBody:
Buying a luxury home, especially for the first time, can be a complex journey with some unique challenges. It’s easy to get swept up in the excitement and overlook critical details that could lead to costly mistakes down the line. Avoiding these common pitfalls can save you significant stress, time, and money, ensuring your first luxury purchase is a rewarding experience. Understanding the nuances of high-value properties, from financing to inspections, is crucial.

Common Mistakes to Avoid:
- [ ] Relying on a standard inspection alone — why it matters: Luxury homes often have pools, elevators, extensive renovations, unique mechanical systems, or coastal exposure that require specialized inspections beyond a general home inspection. Missing these can lead to unexpected repair costs. You should coordinate specialist structural, roof, HVAC, or engineering evaluations as needed.
- [ ] Underestimating reserves and recurring ownership costs — why it matters: Luxury properties come with higher property taxes, insurance, maintenance, and potentially HOA fees. Not budgeting enough for these ongoing expenses can strain your finances. Ensure you account for substantial post-closing reserves.
- [ ] Making large financial changes during underwriting — why it matters: Any significant changes to your income, assets, or debt while your jumbo loan is being underwritten can jeopardize your approval. Keep your financial situation stable until closing.
- [ ] Failing to verify title, boundaries, easements, or property-specific restrictions — why it matters: Complex luxury properties may have specific legal considerations that aren't immediately obvious. A thorough title review is essential to avoid future disputes or limitations on your property use.

How to use this checklist: Go through each item before, during, and after your property search and offer process. Use it as a conversation starter with your real estate professional to ensure all bases are covered.
